name: Bounds Tree Recorded Descent Positions

atomicDiscipline.rule: Run exactly the printed hypothesis. If the attempted change fails, degrades, or suggests a different fix, revert to the checkpoint and finish this experiment as failure. Start a new experiment for the next idea.

primaryTarget: gpux BoundsTree propagation with apps/test_suite wide DataTable headed WebGPU
hypothesisMarkdown:
# Hypothesis

`BoundsTree::insert_leaf` already computes `best_child_pos` at every descent level, but reverse propagation currently discards that position and scans the same fixed child array with `.position(...)` when an increased max order must move the updated child to the end. Retaining `(node_index, child_position)` in the reusable insertion path will remove these repeated scans without changing child selection, swaps, tree shape, or ordering.
measurementPlanMarkdown:
# Measurement plan

1. Change the reusable insertion path entries from node indices to `(node_index, selected_child_position)` and record them after selecting the best child.
2. During reverse propagation, skip terminal-node swapping as today and use each ancestor's recorded child position directly instead of scanning for `updated_child_idx`.
3. Preserve all selection costs, child swaps, max-order updates, tree shape, and public behavior.
4. Run diagnostics-off/on compilation, focused diagnostics, the 1,000-seed ordering oracle, Clippy, nested formatting, and headed WebGPU wide DataTable proof at both DPRs.
5. Accept on the direct removal of ancestor position scans, exact counters/semantics, and non-regressing p95; otherwise revert.
expectedOutcomeMarkdown:
# Expected outcome

All bounds-tree and renderer telemetry remains exact. The insertion path stores one additional `usize` per shallow tree level but reuses its allocation, while propagation no longer performs up-to-12-child equality scans for ancestors whose max order increases. Randomized ordering and headed WebGPU p95 remain unchanged.

playwright: Two candidate processes passed functional assertions across 4/4 headed WebGPU DPR projects, but both repeated throughput degradation.
DPR 2 candidate median throughput fell 6.64% and paced p95 rose 4.21% versus the checkpoint.
rayx: All runtime proof used apps/test_suite; apps/lab was neither launched nor modified.
The 1,000-seed randomized ordering oracle, diagnostics-off/on focused tests, Clippy, and formatting passed before runtime rejection.
The candidate source was reverted exactly to checkpoint before recording failure.
counters: Tree and renderer counters were unchanged, so the regression is attributable to the attempted insertion-path representation trade rather than changed work output.
The tuple doubled each reusable path entry from one usize to two while removing only shallow ancestor scans.

reportMarkdown:
# Bounds tree recorded descent positions report

The candidate changed reusable insertion-path entries from one node index to `(node_index, child_position)` and used the recorded positions to replace ancestor child scans. The 1,000-seed ordering oracle, diagnostics modes, Clippy, formatting, and all headed functional assertions passed, and tree/renderer counters remained exact.

The trade regressed runtime twice. Candidate median throughput was 29.21 steps/s at DPR 1 versus checkpoint 30.21 (-3.31%) and 28.18 at DPR 2 versus 30.18 (-6.64%). Candidate median paced p95 was 27.61 ms at DPR 1 versus 27.32 (+1.07%) and 28.28 ms at DPR 2 versus 27.14 (+4.21%). The doubled path-entry width costs more than the eliminated shallow scans in this workload.

Per AgentX atomic discipline, the candidate source was reverted exactly to checkpoint `f3700c2db` before recording failure. No durable memory or gpux skill guidance was added from this failed attempt.
decisionMarkdown:
# Decision

Reject and revert. Functional equivalence is insufficient: two independent processes repeat lower throughput, with DPR 2 showing a 6.64% throughput loss and 4.21% p95 regression. Retain the compact single-index insertion path and its shallow ancestor scan.
